configurations.name: riskerm
configurations.//: autoPort lets a second session run alongside the first rather than failing on a port the other holds. Nothing here needs a fixed port — no OAuth callback, webhook or CORS origin is pinned to localhost:8123. The sh wrapper is load-bearing: `php artisan serve` reads SERVER_PORT, not PORT (ServeCommand.php), so simply dropping the flag would leave Laravel on its default 8000 while the harness proxied to the assigned port and found nothing — a server that starts, looks healthy and serves no one.
